title: What moc Generates, and the Error When It Does Not

questions.question: Why does a missing Q_OBJECT show up at link time rather than compile time?
options: The macro declares things without defining them, and only the linker notices a missing definition
Because the compiler ignores Qt headers
Because moc runs after linking
Because Q_OBJECT is only checked in release builds
questions.explanation: Declarations satisfy the compiler. The definitions live in moc's generated file, and their absence is a linker problem.

questions.question: What does moc write for each signal you declare?
options: A real function body that packages the arguments and calls every connection
Nothing, signals are handled entirely by the compiler
A slot with a matching name
A thread that waits for the signal to be emitted
questions.explanation: A signal is an ordinary member function whose body moc supplies. That is why an unmoc'd signal is an undefined reference.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three causes of the vtable error?
options: The signal was connected to a slot with a different name
The class is missing Q_OBJECT
moc never saw the header because it is not part of a target
Q_OBJECT was added without reconfiguring the build
questions.explanation: A mismatched connection is a runtime problem that makes connect return false. The vtable error is always about moc not generating code.

questions.question: How do the tests prove moc actually ran, rather than just that the code compiled?
options: They ask the meta object for the class name and for the signal by signature
They measure how long the build took
They check that a moc file exists on disk
They call the signal directly and catch the error
questions.explanation: moc stores names and signatures as text in the meta object, so a class can be interrogated at runtime about what was generated for it.

questions.question: Why does this repository list lesson headers as target sources in CMake?
options: AUTOMOC only processes headers that belong to a target
To make the build faster
Because CMake refuses to build a target without headers
So the headers get installed alongside the binaries
questions.explanation: AUTOMOC scans the target's sources. A header holding Q_OBJECT that is not listed is never handed to moc, and the lesson fails to link.

questions.question: You add Q_OBJECT, rebuild, and the same error appears. What is the most likely reason?
options: The build system is still working from its previous decision, so reconfigure
Q_OBJECT must go at the end of the class
Qt needs to be reinstalled
The class also needs a virtual destructor
questions.explanation: Which files get moc'd is decided at configure time. Adding the macro after that decision needs a reconfigure before it takes effect.
